title: Debug: The Symmetric Difference Is Missing Half Its Rows
description:
This is meant to report every `order_id` out of sync between `source_orders` and `warehouse_orders`, **in either direction**. On some data it looks right, but on data where the two systems are completely disjoint, it's clearly missing rows it should report. Find the bug and fix it.

Name the column `order_id`. Return the result in any order.
hint: Chained set operators (EXCEPT, UNION, INTERSECT) evaluate strictly left-to-right at equal precedence in SQLite — `A EXCEPT B UNION C EXCEPT D` is `((A EXCEPT B) UNION C) EXCEPT D`, not two independent EXCEPTs joined by UNION. Wrap each EXCEPT as its own subquery in FROM to force the grouping you actually want.

tests.name: Example
All three systems fully agree
Completely disjoint across all three
Source has an accidental duplicate row
Only source has any data
tests.seedSql: INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'Ann Lee',120.0),(2,'Ben Kim',80.0),(3,'Cy Ortiz',45.5);

tests.name: Same order, inconsistent name formatting
Matching ids, mismatched amounts
Single matching order everywhere
Larger mixed set: some in all three, some in two, some in one, duplicates and a mismatch
Disjoint data — buggy chain evaluation gives wrong result
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (3,'C',300.0),(4,'D',400.0);

tests.name: All synced — both queries agree (empty result)
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);

tests.name: Partial overlap — buggy chain can give wrong result
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0),(3,'C',300.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (2,'B',200.0),(4,'D',400.0);
